A regulation padel court plays at sixty-five feet seven by thirty-two feet ten. But the concrete pad you build on should be thirty-six by sixty-nine feet. That includes the perimeter ring beam that anchors the court to the concrete.

Headline: TIPS BEFORE YOU BUILD
Tip 1: CHECK SETBACK RULES
Tip 1 sub-line: How far the court must sit from your property lines
Tip 2: RUN IT NORTH-SOUTH
Tip 2 sub-line: Keeps the sun out of players' eyes
Tip 3: SLOPE THE SLAB 0.5-0.7%
Tip 3 sub-line: From one short end to the other, so water drains
Tip 4: WANT LIGHTS? PLAN ACCESS TO YOUR UTILITY BOX

A few tips before you build. Check your city's setback rules: how far the court has to sit from your property lines. Run the court north-south to keep the sun out of players' eyes. Slope the slab half a percent to seven tenths of a percent, from one short end to the other, so water drains. And if you want lights, plan access to your utility box early.

Headline: THE CONCRETE SLAB
Dimension labels: 36' X 69' (11M X 21M)
Area label: 2,484 SQ FT (231 M²)
Cross-section labels: 6" POST-TENSIONED · 4,000 PSI · PITCHED 0.5-1%

Sub-caption: 6-inch post-tensioned slab, at least 4,000 PSI

That footprint is your concrete slab: thirty-six by sixty-nine feet, about twenty-five hundred square feet. We build it six inches thick, post-tensioned, at least four thousand PSI, and pitched slightly so water runs off. Skip this and you'll see cracking, ponding, and turf failures.
